context.title: Last Words and Mighty Men
context.summary: David's last poetic words describe a just ruler as the morning sun and rest on God's everlasting covenant. A roll of David's mighty men follows, with stories of their courage and the three who risked their lives to bring him water from Bethlehem's well.
context.background: David calls himself 'the sweet psalmist of Israel' (v. 1). When his men brought water through the Philistine lines, he refused to drink it and poured it out to the Lord, because it had cost the risk of their lives (vv. 16–17). The list of heroes ends pointedly with 'Uriah the Hittite' (v. 39).

customs.term: Poured it out unto the Lord
customs.note: A drink offering. David treats water won at such risk as too precious to drink himself.

watchFor: A ruler 'must be just, ruling in the fear of God' (v. 3).
'An everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure' (v. 5).
The final name on the honor roll (v. 39).

w: will he give to drink me

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Adino
people.summary: The Eznite, one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:8).

people.name: Dodo
people.summary: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, who was one of David’s three heroes (2 Sam. 23:9; 1 Chr. 11:12).

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

people.name: Agee
people.summary: Fugitive, the father of Shammah, who was one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11)

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of David’s three mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11, 12).

people.name: Joab
people.summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15).

people.name: Zeruiah
people.summary: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

people.name: Abishai
people.summary: Father of (i.e., “desirous of”) a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel (2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chr. 2:16).

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: The son of Jehoiada, chief priest (1 Chr. 27:5). He was set by David over his body-guard of Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 1:32; 1 Chr. 18:17).

people.name: Jehoiada
people.summary: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

people.name: Asahel
people.summary: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle (2 Sam. 2:18, 19).

people.name: Dodo
people.summary: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

people.name: Elhanan
people.summary: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of David’s mighties (2 Sam. 23:25); called also Shammoth (1 Chr. 11:27) and Shamhuth (27:8).

people.name: Elika
people.summary: God is his rejector, one of David’s thirty-seven distinguished heros (2 Sam. 23:25).

people.name: Helez
people.summary: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

people.name: Ira
people.summary: A Tekoite, one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

people.name: Sibbechai
people.summary: The Lord sustains, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:29), general of the eighth division of the army (27:11). He slew the giant Saph in the battle of Gob (2 Sam. 21:18; R.V., “Sibbechai”).

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:27; comp. 1 Chr. 27:12).

people.name: Ilai
people.summary: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Heleb
people.summary: Fatness, one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:29).

people.name: Baanah
people.summary: The father of Heled, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29; 1 Chr. 11:30).

people.name: Ittai
people.summary: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

people.name: Hurai
people.summary: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

people.name: Azmaveth
people.summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:31).

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: Eliahba the Shaalbonite.

people.name: Jashen
people.summary: Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).

people.name: Ahiam
people.summary: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:33; 1 Chr. 11:35).

people.name: Sharar
people.summary: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:35); called also Sharar (2 Sam. 23:33).

people.name: Ahithophel
people.summary: Brother of insipidity or impiety, a man greatly renowned for his sagacity among the Jews. At the time of Absalom’s revolt he deserted David (Ps. 41:9; 55:12-14) and espoused the cause of Absalom (2 Sam. 15:12).

people.name: Eliam
people.summary: This name also occurs as that of a Gilonite, the son of Ahithophel, and one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:34). perhaps these two were the same person.

people.name: Eliphelet
people.summary: One of David’s distinguished warriors (2 Sam. 23:34); called also Eliphal in 1 Chr. 11:35.

people.name: Hezrai
people.summary: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

people.name: Paarai
people.summary: Opening of the Lord, “the Arbite,” one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:35); called also Naarai, 1 Chr. 11:37.

people.name: Bani
people.summary: One of David’s thirty-seven warriors, a Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

people.name: Igal
people.summary: Son of Nathan of Zobah, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:36).

people.name: Naharai
people.summary: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

people.name: Zelek
people.summary: Cleft, an Ammonite; one of David’s valiant men (2 Sam. 23:37).

people.name: Gareb
people.summary: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

people.name: Ira
people.summary: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

people.name: Uriah
people.summary: A Hittite, the husband of Bathsheba, whom David first seduced, and then after Uriah’s death married. He was one of the band of David’s “mighty men.”

places.name: Adullam
places.summary: One of the royal cities of the Canaanites, now ‘Aid-el-ma (Josh. 12:15; 15:35). It stood on the old Roman road in the valley of Elah, which was the scene of David’s memorable victory over Goliath (1 Sam. 17:2), and not far from Gath.

places.name: valley of Rephaim
places.summary: (Josh. 15:8; 18:16, R.V.). When David became king over all Israel, the Philistines, judging that he would now become their uncompromising enemy, made a sudden attack upon Hebron, compelling David to retire from it.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city in the “hill country” of Judah. It was originally called Ephrath (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7; Ruth 4:11). It was also called Beth-lehem Ephratah (Micah 5:2), Beth-lehem-judah (1 Sam. 17:12), and “the city of David” (Luke 2:4).

places.name: Kabzeel
places.summary: Gathering of God, a city in the extreme south of Judah, near to Idumaea (Josh. 15:21), the birthplace of Benaiah, one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 23:20; 1 Chr. 11:22).

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Harod
places.summary: An epithet applied to two of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:25).

places.name: Netophah
places.summary: Distillation; dropping, a town in Judah, in the neighbourhood, probably, of Bethlehem (Neh. 7:26; 1 Chr. 2:54). Two of David’s guards were Netophathites (1 Chr. 27:13, 15).

places.name: Gibeah
places.summary: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” (1 Sam. 13:15), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; Isa. 10:29). It was here that the terrible outrage was committed on the Levite’s concubine which led to the almost utter extirpation of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 19; 20), only six hundred men surviving after a succession of disastrous battles.

places.name: Gaash
places.summary: A shaking, a hill, on the north side of which Joshua was buried (Josh. 24:30; Judg. 2:9), in the territory of Ephraim.

places.name: Pirathon
places.summary: Prince, or summit, a place “in the land of Ephraim” (Judg. 12:15), now Fer’on, some 10 miles south-west of Shechem.

places.name: Bahurim
places.summary: Young men, a place east of Jerusalem (2 Sam. 3:16; 19:16), on the road to the Jordan valley.

places.name: Gilo
places.summary: A name given to Hashem, an inhabitant of Gizoh, a place somewhere in the mountains of Judah (1 Chr. 11:34; 2 Sam. 23:32, 34).

places.name: Maacah
places.summary: Oppression, a small Syrian kingdom near Geshur, east of the Hauran, the district of Batanea (Josh. 13:13; 2 Sam. 10:6, 8; 1 Chr. 19:7).

places.name: Carmel
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:55), the residence of Nabal (1 Sam. 25:2, 5, 7, 40), and the native place of Abigail, who became David’s wife (1 Sam. 27:3).

places.name: Zobah
places.summary: Aram-Zobah, (Ps. 60, title), a Syrian province or kingdom to the south of Coele-Syria, and extending from the eastern slopes of Lebanon north and east toward the Euphrates.

places.name: Beeroth
places.summary: Wells, one of the four cities of the Hivites which entered by fraud into a league with Joshua. It belonged to Benjamin (Josh. 18:25).

events.title: Reign of David
events.summary: Passage: 2 Samuel 2:1–24:25. People: David. Place: Hebron, Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
